reason: Multiple independent sources corroborate more than a dozen key claims regarding Haumea's discovery, rapid rotation, elongated shape, ring system, moons, and surface features.
story: Far out in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune orbits Haumea, one of the strangest worlds in our solar system. Discovered from observations in 2003 and 2004 and originally nicknamed 'Santa', Haumea takes about 285 Earth years to circle the Sun. Yet this dwarf planet completes a full rotation every 3.9 hours, making it one of the fastest-spinning large objects in the solar system. The intense centrifugal force stretches this rocky, ice-coated world into the shape of a triaxial ellipsoid resembling an elongated football. Scientists believe a massive collision billions of years ago sent Haumea into its frantic spin and blasted off material that formed its two moons, Hi'iaka and Namaka. In 2017, watching Haumea pass in front of a distant star revealed another shock: a crisp ring system encircling the dwarf planet, the first ever found around a Kuiper Belt object.
angle: Haumea spins so violently fast—a full day takes under four hours—that the dwarf planet has been stretched into the shape of a celestial football and is ringed by its own cosmic debris.

claims.claim: Haumea is a dwarf planet orbiting in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune.
One discovery team nicknamed the object 'Santa'.
Two separate teams claimed credit for discovering Haumea based on observations from 2003 and 2004.
The dwarf planet is named after the Hawaiian goddess of fertility.
Haumea takes approximately 285 Earth years to complete one orbit around the Sun.
Haumea rotates once roughly every 3.9 to 4 hours.
Haumea is one of the fastest-rotating large objects in the solar system.
Haumea's rapid rotation has distorted it into an elongated, football-like triaxial ellipsoid.
Haumea's composition consists predominantly of rock coated by a layer of ice.
A giant collision billions of years ago likely spun up Haumea and created its moons.
Haumea has two known moons, named Hi'iaka and Namaka.
Both of Haumea's moons were discovered in 2005.
Hi'iaka is the outer moon, while Namaka is the inner moon.
Astronomers discovered a ring system orbiting Haumea, announced in 2017.
Haumea's ring was detected when the dwarf planet passed in front of a star.
Haumea was the first trans-Neptunian object known to possess a ring system.
A dark red spot richer in minerals and organic compounds than the surrounding ice was detected on Haumea's surface.

disputed: Discovery credit: Mike Brown's Caltech team accused Ortiz Moreno's Spanish team of fraud after Ortiz accessed Caltech logs before announcing the discovery; the IAU lists Sierra Nevada Observatory as the discovery site but lists no official discoverer and chose the Caltech team's proposed name. Script should attribute: 'Two teams claimed discovery credit amid controversy, leading the IAU to credit the Spanish observatory for location while adopting the American team's proposed name.'

Haumea's exact dimensions and hydrostatic equilibrium: Pre-2017 models estimated dimensions around 2,000 x 1,500 x 1,000 km in hydrostatic equilibrium, whereas 2017 occultation measurements indicated a larger longest axis and challenged whether it is in hydrostatic equilibrium. Script should present the shape as an elongated triaxial ellipsoid without insisting on exact kilometer dimensions.
